question.problem:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the following probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{2-x}, & x\ge 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

If the probability density function of $Y=(X-4)^{2}$ is given by 

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}g(y), & 0<y<4 \\ h(y), & y\ge 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

find the function $g(y).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's visualize the transformation $Y=(X-4)^{2}$ over the interval $x\ge 2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14231916/assets/77008820197d69dc81d674a48e207b7527d2f3d4cc1d0ca3ed8ad4d8553665b8.png)

Notice the following:

- The transformation is two-to-one over the interval $2<x<6.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $0<y<4.$

- The transformation is one-to-one over the interval $x\ge 6.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $y\ge 4.$

In this question, we're asked to consider only the interval $0<y<4.$

Using the definition of the cumulative distribution of $Y,$ for $0<y<4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & =P(Y\le y) \\  & =P((X-4)^{2}\le y) \\  & =P(-\sqrt{y}\le X-4\le \sqrt{y}) \\  & =P(4-\sqrt{y}\le X\le 4+\sqrt{y}) \\  & ={F}_{X}(4+\sqrt{y})-{F}_{X}(4-\sqrt{y}).\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the PDF ${f}_{Y}(y)$ for $0<y<4,$ we differentiate ${F}_{Y}$ with respect to $y$ using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={F}_{Y}^{′}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {F}_{X}^{′}(4+\sqrt{y})+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {F}_{X}^{′}(4-\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {f}_{X}(4+\sqrt{y})+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {f}_{X}(4-\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}({f}_{X}(4+\sqrt{y})+{f}_{X}(4-\sqrt{y})).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the definition of ${f}_{X},$ we finally arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}({f}_{X}(4+\sqrt{y})+{f}_{X}(4-\sqrt{y})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}({e}^{2-4-\sqrt{y}}+{e}^{2-4+\sqrt{y}}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-\sqrt{y}-2}+{e}^{\sqrt{y}-2}}{2\sqrt{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $g(y)=\frac{{e}^{-\sqrt{y}-2}+{e}^{\sqrt{y}-2}}{2\sqrt{y}}.$
